slides.heading: Year 1 — Autumn 1, Week 4
slides.sub: New content taught directly, practised in words/sentences and applied in reading and dictation.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "wh" (/w/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="whale" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="whale"><path d="M-22 0q14 -16 44 0q-30 16 -44 0z" fill="#e2483f" stroke="#5c0f0c" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M-22 0l-14 -10v20z" fill="#e2483f" stroke="#5c0f0c" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="14" cy="-3" r="3" fill="#1d2b38" stroke="none"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Whisper the Feather floats wherever the wind takes her, asking a soft 'wh, wh' as she drifts past.

character.name: Whisper the Feather
character.blurb: Whisper the Feather is a pale sky-coloured feather who drifts on the breeze, whispering 'wh' every time the wind changes.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'w' in web — the 'h' stays silent and mostly tags along in question words.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'w', then 'h', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children blow softly onto their open hand, as if blowing a feather, while whispering 'wh'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="whale" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="whale"><path d="M-22 0q14 -16 44 0q-30 16 -44 0z" fill="#e2483f" stroke="#5c0f0c" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M-22 0l-14 -10v20z" fill="#e2483f" stroke="#5c0f0c" stroke-width="2.5"/><circle cx="14" cy="-3" r="3" fill="#1d2b38" stroke="none"/></svg>

slides.dictation: A fair has a big wheel.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ph" (/f/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="elephant" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="elephant_j"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Delphine Pinecone rattles her scales together and puffs out a breathy 'ph' whenever she's asked a question, as if she's answering the phone.

character.name: Delphine Pinecone
character.blurb: Delphine Pinecone is a deep berry-coloured pinecone speckled with spots, and she puffs a soft 'ph' sound out through her scales.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'f' in fan — 'ph' often appears in longer, more grown-up words.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'p', then 'h', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children hold a flat hand near their mouth like a phone and puff out a soft 'ph' sound.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="elephant" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="elephant_j"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: A dolphin leaps out of the sea.

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ve" (/v/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="dove" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="dove"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: No word likes to end in v, so an e comes along to finish it — give, live, sleeve. Even Olive's name ends this way.
slides.pronunciation_note: The /v/ sound children already know from 'van'. English words hardly ever end in the letter v, so when a word ends with a /v/ sound, an e is added after the v and makes no sound: give, live, have, sleeve.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'v', then 'e', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children rest two fingers on their lips and buzz 'vvv', then flick the fingers away for the quiet e.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
